thread:
jia: Quick heads-up — canary rolled kernel-routing tweak that prioritizes int4 quant kernels. After ~30m we're seeing ~8-12% host CPU P95 regression on small requests, mostly p95 tails. attaching quick notes and a flame sample.

liam: saw the alert. flame points at preparse/tokenizer + grpc writev hot paths, not the GPU.

rachel: curious — kvcache hit-rate changed? routing to a different shard could spike misses.

jia: kvcache hit rate looks flat (98% on the canary set). this looks like extra syscalls in request parsing + more small writev calls. pasted snippet from perf:```perf top -p 2345 -n | head
  1.2%  libc-2.31.so  [.] syscall
  1.1%  runtime       [.] parse_request
  0.9%  runtime       [.] tokenize_chunk
  0.6%  grpc_core     [.] writev_coalesce
```

maya: interesting. did we change http/2 framing logic when we flipped kernel routing? small writes / single-token responses are sensitive to write coalescing.

ops-bot: canary-deploy: 6529001100 -> traffic 50% -> health OK (but increased host cpu p95).

liam: quick repro worked locally with wrk: many small completions show same tail. try toggling writev coalesce and tokenization pool.

jia: plan: add lightweight sampling to measure parse+tokenize latency by response-size bucket, and measure number of writev calls per request. if regression >5% rollback kernel-priority. @rachel can you run a live pprof on node-3 and capture allocation stacks?

rachel: on it. also prepping a micro-patch to avoid per-token mallocs in tokenizer (use arena). will push for canary tomorrow.

maya: I'll test toggling grpc write coalescing knob on the canary (decrease flush microthreshold) and re-run perf. will also try forcing CPU affinity so kernel selection stays same but ingress path reverts.

jia: thanks — next steps: (1) pprof capture from rachel, (2) maya runs coalesce knob test, (3) liam prepares revert if >5% reg keeps for 1h. keep updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
